reason: AirPay's payment API defines the form checksum as hex MD5 of the buyer fields, amount, order id, date and private key. AirPay accepts no other algorithm; the result itself is verified with AirPay's own secure hash. Not used anywhere else.

Bank of Maldives and HNB Sentry (MPI protocol) define the request and response Signature as Base64 SHA-1 of the password and fields (SignatureMethod=SHA1). The banks accept no other algorithm; a different hash breaks those payments. Not used anywhere else.

GoPES's init-payment API requires the merchant key and password encrypted with PBKDF2 + AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding. AviQR only encrypts and sends; it never decrypts attacker-supplied data, so there is no padding oracle.
